jobs.description:
The Department of Clinical Medicine at the Faculty of Health, Aarhus University, invites applications for a position as AI Developer for validation and clinical implementation of AI systems, commencing on 1 January 2027, preferably before then, if possible. The position is a fixed-term full-time appointment until 31 December 2028 which aligns with the end date of the project related to the grant agreement. 

AURA is the radiology research unit at Aarhus University Hospital and is affiliated with the Department of Clinical Medicine at Aarhus University. We conduct research across a broad range of radiological topics and work closely with clinical departments on projects spanning classical statistical methods, artificial intelligence, language models, and advanced image analysis.

In recent years, we have expanded our activities within AI and are therefore seeking additional expertise for both existing and new projects. As an AI Developer in AURA, you will play a central role in validating, implementing, and further developing AI solutions for use in healthcare. You will become part of an ambitious research environment with close collaboration between researchers, clinicians, and technical specialists, and you will have the opportunity to influence both projects and your own role.

As an AI Developer at the Department of Clinical Medicine, you will become part of what is likely the largest health sciences research institute in Denmark. Clinical research covers all medical specialties and is carried out in close collaboration with the university hospital and regional hospitals in the Central Denmark Region. We have approximately 30,000 square metres of modern research facilities for experimental surgery and medicine, animal facilities, and advanced scanners. The department has overall responsibility for the Master’s degree programmes in Medicine and Molecular Medicine. The department comprises approximately 670 academic staff members, 500 PhD students, and 160 technical and administrative staff, all working collaboratively across disciplines. As an AI Developer, you will be based at Aarhus University Hospital in the Central Denmark Region. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your Job Responsibilities
As an AI Developer, your primary responsibilities will be to develop, validate, and implement AI solutions for clinical use, while supporting the research group's activities within data analysis, software development, and advanced image analysis. You will contribute to research and development activities through technical development, project work, and interdisciplinary collaboration. In your daily work, you will collaborate closely with researchers, clinicians, students, and external partners.

Your tasks will primarily include:

• Validation and implementation of AI systems for clinical use.
• Development, testing, and evaluation of new AI solutions.
• Software development and data analysis related to research and development projects.
• Establishment and maintenance of technical workflows and development environments.
• Responsibility for your own technical sub-projects and development processes.
• Providing technical and methodological support and advice to researchers and clinicians.
• Co-supervision and academic support of Master's and PhD students.
• Collaboration with external partners, including companies and healthcare stakeholders.
• Contributing to the establishment of new research and development projects within AI and radiology.
The position offers a high degree of independence, and we would like you to help shape the content of the role so that it matches your competencies, interests, and career goals.

You will report to Clinical Professor, Department Chair of Radiology, Ole Graumann.

Your Qualifications
You hold a Master's degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, software development, physics, engineering, or a related discipline.

We expect that you:

• Have strong competencies in programming and software development.
• Are familiar with Linux and command-line based work.
• Have experience with AI development or similar technical development work.
• Are able to work independently and drive technical projects and sub-projects.
• Enjoy collaborating with and supporting researchers and students in their projects.
It is an advantage if you have experience with:

• Research projects or research collaborations.
• Healthcare data, medical image analysis, or clinical AI systems.
• Supervision, teaching, or academic mentoring.
Your educational background is less important than your technical competencies, experience, and ability to translate technical solutions into practical applications within a clinical environment.

As a person, you possess strong collaborative skills, demonstrate initiative, and are able to drive progress in complex projects. You thrive in an interdisciplinary environment and contribute positively to a good working environment. We expect you to speak and write English fluently.

We Offer
• A strong and ambitious research environment with close ties to clinical practice.
• Significant influence over your own projects and responsibilities.
• The opportunity to shape the development and implementation of AI solutions in healthcare.
• The opportunity to co-supervise Master's and PhD students.
• Excellent opportunities for professional development within AI, software development, and clinical implementation.
• An interdisciplinary environment with close collaboration between researchers, clinicians, and technical specialists.
Questions About the Position
If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact MD, PhD, and External Lecturer Mathis Rasmussen by telephone at +45 23 80 42 10 or by email at mathis.rasmussen@rm.dk.

The place of work is AURA, Department of Radiology, Aarhus University Hospital, Palle Juul-Jensens Boulevard 99, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

The application deadline is Monday the 9th of November 2026.

We expect to conduct interviews Monday the 23rd of November 2026. A second interview, if required, is expected to take place on Wednesday, 25th of November 2026. As part of the recruitment process, you may be asked to complete a short professional case assignment.

Terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment are governed by the collective agreement for Academics in the State, Nurses in the State or Nurses and radiographers with a master’s degree. Academics in the State will be appointed at basic salary grade 4–8. For the right candidate, appointment as Senior Consultant will be possible, with remuneration in accordance with Appendix 4 of the collective agreement. Nurses in the State will be appointed at basic salary grade 1-6, and Nurses and radiographers with a master’s degree will be appointed at basic salary grade 1-8.

Application

We refer to the faculty’s Guideline for applicants.

jobs.occupation: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
jobs.description:
Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring.

This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. 

Job description
The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere.

You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics.

Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage.

Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. 

What we offer 
The successful candidate is offered:

• Access to a well-developed research infrastructure
• Office space and shared equipment
• a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Måske brænder du særligt for tyskfaget og den sproglige formidling, og måske har du også andre kompetencer og interesser, som kan bringes i spil i skolens hverdag. Vi vil gerne i dialog med dig om, hvordan vi sammen kan skabe en stilling, der giver mening for både dig og vores elever.

Om stillingen

• Undervisning i tysk i udskolingen.
• Mulighed for at præge og udvikle undervisningen med dine egne idéer og faglige interesser.
• Mulighed for en deltids- eller fuldtidsstilling afhængigt af dine kompetencer og ønsker.
• Mulighed for at bringe andre relevante kompetencer i spil og være med til at forme stillingens indhold.
• En arbejdsplads med fokus på faglig udvikling, stærke relationer og gode fællesskaber blandt elever og medarbejdere.
 

Vores børnesyn – alle børn skal have mulighed for at lykkes

På Brøndbyvester Skole arbejder vi ud fra et fælles børnesyn:

”Børn og unge gør det bedste, de kan, med de kompetencer, de har. Det er de voksnes ansvar at inddrage børn og unge i positive fællesskaber og læringsmiljøer med lige adgang til at udfolde og udvikle sig og trives.”

Det betyder, at vi møder børn og unge med nysgerrighed, respekt og positive forventninger. Vi tror på, at alle elever har potentiale til at udvikle sig, og at det er vores ansvar som voksne at skabe rammerne for, at de kan lykkes både fagligt, socialt og personligt.

Som lærer hos os er du med til at skabe et trygt og motiverende læringsmiljø, hvor eleverne oplever, at de bliver set, hørt og taget alvorligt. Vi ved, at børn er forskellige, og at de har brug for forskellige tilgange, udfordringer og former for støtte. Derfor er det vigtigt, at du kan tilpasse din undervisning og skabe plads til både forskellighed og fællesskab.

I tyskundervisningen får du mulighed for at vække elevernes nysgerrighed på sprog og kultur, skabe mod på at prøve sig frem og vise dem, at det er en del af læringen at begå fejl. Vi ønsker, at eleverne oplever tysk som et levende sprog, de kan bruge til at forstå verden omkring sig.

Vi forestiller os, at du …

• Er læreruddannet og har erfaring med at undervise i tysk i grundskolen.
• Brænder for formidling og kan gøre undervisningen engagerende, varieret og vedkommende.
• Er relationskompetent og kan skabe trygge rammer, hvor eleverne tør deltage og udvikle sig.
• Møder eleverne med anerkendelse, tydelighed og positive forventninger.
• Kan tilpasse undervisningen til elevernes forskellige forudsætninger og behov.
• Har lyst til at samarbejde med kolleger om elevernes faglige udvikling, trivsel og deltagelse i fællesskabet.
 

Hvad kan vi tilbyde dig?

På Brøndbyvester Skole bliver du en del af en arbejdsplads, hvor faglighed, fællesskab og trivsel går hånd i hånd. Vi prioriterer et tæt samarbejde mellem kolleger og ledelse og ønsker at skabe rammer, hvor medarbejdernes idéer, initiativer og faglige interesser kan komme til udtryk. Brøndbyvester Skole er en stor skole fordelt på to matrikler. Denne stilling er tilknyttet afdeling Tornehøj, hvor vi har elever fra 5.-9. klasse. Her bliver du en del af et læringsmiljø, hvor samarbejde, faglig udvikling og gode relationer er vigtige elementer i hverdagen. Det vigtigste er ikke, at du kan det hele fra begyndelsen, men at du har lyst til at gøre en forskel for vores elever og bidrage positivt til fællesskabet. 

Vi vil gerne skabe en stilling, hvor du får mulighed for at bringe dine styrker i spil, udvikle dine faglige interesser og få indflydelse på din hverdag. Vi tror på, at de bedste løsninger opstår i dialog, og derfor er vi nysgerrige på, hvad du kan bidrage med, og hvordan vi sammen kan få dine kompetencer til at blomstre.

Praktisk information og ansøgning

• Ansøgningsfrist: onsdag den 11. november.
• Samtaler: Vi afholder samtaler løbende, så send gerne din ansøgning hurtigst muligt.
Vil du være med?

Hvis du kan se dig selv som en del af Brøndbyvester Skole, glæder vi os til at høre fra dig. Fortæl os gerne om din faglige baggrund, dine interesser og dine tanker om god undervisning og om, hvordan du kunne tænke dig at sætte dit præg på stillingen.

Har du spørgsmål eller vil du høre mere om mulighederne, er du meget velkommen til at kontakte skoleleder Laila Sevgi Holme på telefon 21768543.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig og til måske at byde dig velkommen i fællesskabet på Brøndbyvester Skole!

 

 

Søg stillingen via 'ansøg'-knappen. Her kan du uploade din ansøgning og CV samt evt. relevant dokumentation. 

Alle interesserede ansøgere uanset alder, køn, handicap, religion eller etnisk tilhørsforhold opfordres til at søge stillingen.

Brøndby Kommune har røgfri arbejdstid. 

Brøndby er en centralt beliggende hovedstadskommune med cirka 40.000 indbyggere. Byens puls er præget af fællesskab, mangfoldighed og en stærk idrætskultur. Vi er en kommune med kant og spændende kontraster med bolig- og erhvervsområder, skove, grønne områder og Strandparken med havet og indsøerne.

Senior Project Manager – Clean & Industrial Utilities

Location: Hillerød, Denmark

Department: DPM Expansion – Future QC

Are you ready to take ownership of a critical utilities workstream within one of Novo's largest quality control expansion projects?

Do you bring strong experience in clean or industrial utilities, combined with a practical understanding of commissioning, qualification and project delivery?

Are you motivated by the opportunity to influence a major Greenfield development, work with experienced engineering specialists and take responsibility for delivering complex technical systems?

If you enjoy combining technical knowledge with project leadership, stakeholder collaboration and practical problem solving, this could be an exciting next step in your career.

We are looking for a Senior Project Manager Clean & Industrial Utilities to join our DPM Expansion – Future QC programme in Hillerod, Denmark.

The position

As Senior Project Manager, you will take ownership of the commissioning and qualification planning and coordination for clean and industrial utility systems within our new Future QC facility.

The project represents an investment of approximately DKK 3 billion and involves the construction of a 42,000 m² quality control laboratory facility, the largest of its kind within Novo.

Working within a relatively lean and highly collaborative project organisation, you will have significant responsibility and the opportunity to make a direct impact on how critical utility systems are delivered, qualified and handed over to operations.

A central part of your role will be ensuring that commissioning and qualification activities are effectively planned, coordinated and aligned with construction milestones, equipment installation requirements and phased building handovers.

You will work closely with contractors, engineering specialists, validation colleagues, IT, equipment owners and other project stakeholders to manage technical dependencies, identify risks and ensure the successful progression of the utilities workstream.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead the planning and coordination of commissioning and qualification activities for clean and industrial utility systems.

• Work closely with the validation team to establish qualification strategies, timelines, vendor documentation requirements and appropriate levels of technical oversight.

• Work closely with the validation team to establish qualification strategies, timelines, vendor documentation requirements and appropriate levels of technical oversight.

• Coordinate with the main contractor, subcontractors and engineering specialists to ensure utility systems are delivered in accordance with project requirements and relevant standards.

• Manage interfaces and dependencies between utility availability, equipment installation, controlled shutdowns and phased building handovers.

• Review commissioning and qualification plans, identify potential technical or operational risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

• Engage with equipment owners, IT, engineering and operational stakeholders to understand system requirements and ensure utility availability is aligned with their delivery schedules.

• Provide informed technical recommendations, support decision-making and escalate matters affecting cost, scope or programme timelines through established governance processes.

• Contribute to the successful handover of utility systems to the operational and maintenance organisations.

• Collaborate across the wider project team, supporting other critical workstreams where priorities and project needs require.

• This is a project manager position rather than a detailed engineering design role.

Qualifications

To succeed in this role, you will bring a strong technical foundation in utility systems, practical experience in regulated operational environments and the ability to manage complex engineering activities.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have developed their careers through technical, maintenance, facilities or operational engineering roles before progressing into project management.

We expect you to have:

• A relevant educational background in engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical industry experience.

• Strong technical experience in either clean utilities or industrial utilities, particularly piping related systems such as purified water, clean steam, heating, cooling, water distribution or compressed air.

• Demonstrable experience in equipment or systems commissioning, qualification and/or validation, including a sound understanding of controlled processes, documentation and operational requirements.

• Practical experience working within an operational plant, manufacturing facility or similarly complex technical environment, including exposure to maintenance activities, system start ups, shutdowns or equipment qualification.

• Proven experience coordinating engineering projects, technical workstreams, contractors or specialist service providers.

Experience working within regulated or process driven industries where safety, quality, documentation and controlled operating procedures are essential.

• Strong planning, coordination and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and technical dependencies.

• The ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and spoken.

• Experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing, biotechnology or other GMP regulated environments would be advantageous but is not essential.

• We also welcome relevant experience from industries such as food and beverage, chemical manufacturing, oil and gas, and engineering or EPC organisations, provided you bring the necessary utilities and qualification expertise.

Joining us means contributing to a technically challenging Greenfield project where your experience, judgement and decisions will make a visible difference.

jobs.occupation: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
jobs.description:
About the position
 The Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).

  The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.

  As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.

  The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

  Key responsibilities

  Strategic leadership and governance

   	
• Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates. 	
• Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability. 	
• Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.   Management, organisation and budget

   	
• Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state. 	
• Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices. 	
• Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.   Operational responsibility

   	
• Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication. 	
• Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.   About you
 To succeed in this role, we expect that you:

   	
• Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage. 	
• Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level. 	
• Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions. 	
• Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally. 	
• Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.   In addition, you:

   	
• Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations. 	
• Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries. 	
• Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.   About the Danish Resilience Agency
 The Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.

  We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.

  About the NBCC
 The NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.

  The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.

  As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.

  Salary and terms of employment
 Salary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.

  Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.

  The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.

  The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.

  To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in fungal genomics and predictive modelling - DTU Food
jobs.description:
Fungi are increasingly causing health issues globally. Such infections are not only increasing in humans and animals, but also in crops and as contamination of food products with mycotoxins.

We have recently been awarded funding to develop online webservices for genomic characterization of all pathogens capable of infecting animals, humans and plants, which includes fungi. However, genomics methods and workflows have so far not gained enough attention in relation to plant infecting or mycotoxin producing fungi. 

Databases of genomes of known fungal species have already been developed, as has gene databases of mycotoxin producing gene clusters, but an extensive linkage to fungal taxa is poorly described. Furthermore, it is known that a number of fungi including some used in food production have the gene cluster for mycotoxin production but do not express them.

There is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the genomics of fungi, as well as to translate this into online services.

Thus, as part of our GPAP project (www.gpap.global) and our responsibilities as advise provider to the Danish Food Administration we are seeking a PhD-candidate in fungal genomics with a focus on correlating genomes to phenotypes and developing webservices. This will include whole genome sequencing of fungi, culturing and phenotypic characterization and implementing tools in our widely used online webservice.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to create a webservice for identifying fungal taxa, mycotoxin-producing gene clusters and predict phenotypes under different growth conditions. You will perform complete genome sequencing (including the analyses) of a selected range of fungal to create an improved database of reference genomes.

You will also:

• develop a web-based tool for species identification and detection of known toxin-gene clusters, virulence genes and regulatory genes.
• conduct phenotype to genotype association studies based on a large collection of phenotypically characterized Fusarium isolates and develop and improve the online tool.
• With assistant from other group members, you will analyse the output, draw conclusions and present the outputs. 
• communicate research results by presenting data at project meetings and international conferences and write reports and manuscripts for publication.
• engage in the general work carried out by the research group, including discussions and planning of strategies and projects, drafting research grant proposals, etc.
Daily work will be in close collaboration with other researchers in the Genomic Epidemiology group at DTU Food and the Applied Mycology group at DTU Bioengineering, as well as national and international partners.

The ideal candidate has experience in coding in python and experience with Unix-based systems and in machine and deep learning.

Other desired qualifications are:

• extensive knowledge in microbial genomics including phylogenetic analysis
• extensive knowledge of existing bioinformatic algorithms and tools.
• experience with DNA-based workload from microbes
It is a great advantage if you have experience in general microbiology and preferably fungal culturing.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
The position is a collaboration between DTU Food and DTU Bioengineering, with the employment at DTU-Food. Further information may be obtained from Associate professor Christian Brinch, cbri@food.dtu.dk or Associate professor Jakob Blæsbjerg Hoof, jblni@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU National Food Institute at DTU National Food Institute and DTU Bioengineering at DTU Bioengineering .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• Curriculum vitae

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

You will combine power system engineering, data analytics and applied research to develop methods and tools that support system stability and the management of critical power system events.

Join our power system specialists

At our head office in Fredericia you join a department responsible for supporting the secure and stable operation of the Danish power system, both today and in the future with an increasing share of renewable energy. We develop methods, analyses and digital solutions that support system stability, security of supply and the handling of major disturbances.  As part of Energinet’s System Operations organisation, we work closely with the Control Centre, IT specialists and international transmission system operators.

Develop methods and tools for system stability

You contribute to developing next-generation dynamic stability assessment, system monitoring, and power system restoration capabilities for an electricity system increasingly based on renewable energy.

• analysing power system dynamics, stability and disturbance events using PowerFactory and PSCAD
• developing and applying methods based on PMU and other operational measurement data
